audio_caption: The clip starts with men's voices, one uttering "Langsam, langsam, er kommt doch früh genug dran" in a firm tone, followed by the sound of a door knock. Another man replies, "Was gibt's?", then tells someone to stop with the nonsense and treat him with respect, ordering them to step away. A poignant melody, likely from a string instrument, begins, accompanying a man expressing gratitude. The melody lingers as someone offers a cigarette.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker in a polite but assertive tone, remarking, "You know, if you just walked up to this house in a normal way," explaining how the person would have been invited to lunch. He continues speaking, noting he has "anticipated the pleasure of meeting you for years," then expresses that he doesn't know who he's speaking to. A male speaker with a similar tone then interjects by stating that he likes the other person.

The clip begins with a male speaker describing his passion for big game hunting, suggesting he could have been more famous than the person he's addressing if he hadn't chosen politics. The speaker notes that his branch of politics is a more exciting field of action. He mentions being in Nairobi during the year the other person's exploits were known in Kenya, indicating that he would know who they are. The speaker then says "yes" and mentions "my passport," at which point he is cut off by another male speaker who notes that he would have recognized him on sight.

The clip begins with a male speaker referring to someone's brother who was a guest in the house, followed by a statement that the listener knows his brother.  Another male speaker mentions that "Lord Risborough was sent here by your prime minister on a mission of appeasement." The first male speaker then asserts that he found Risborough a "credulous simpleton," and that "this is the most closely guarded house in the world."

The audio clip begins with a male speaker who sounds calm, as he discusses how he would have wagered his life that no living thing could have entered the area unnoticed, but that he didn't count upon a creature that has learned to stalk even the most cunning animal, moving through a forest as if they were transparent. He points out that in a 500-yard radius, anyone running would be cut down quickly, yet someone was on the ledge above, demonstrating a high degree of skill. Then, a different male speaker replies, seeming surprised at the suggestion that he's an assassin, and explains that he was stopped before he could shoot, but could have easily. He insists he never intended to shoot, but merely wanted to see if it was possible. He says that fellow jumping him made his gun go off. The first speaker ends the clip, seemingly disappointed in the other man.

The clip starts with one male speaker conceding he's been "a bit thick," explaining that he assumed the other person knew it was a sporting stalk. He then asks, "A what? A sporting stalk?". He explains what a sporting stalk is. Another male speaker responds, saying he is not begging off any consequences but doubts the first speaker's claims as a big game hunter. The first speaker interjects, emphasizing that this is the most dangerous of all animals, "Man". The first speaker continues, explaining that you don't kill, "the sport is in the chase, not the kill." The speaker says that he doesn't kill anymore, not even small game, and explains his hunting philosophy. The second male speaker then says that the first speaker's conversation fascinates him, but he finds the softness in his nature regarding the ultimate purpose of firearms concerning.

The clip begins with a male speaker, with a stern tone, criticizing someone's weakness and decadence, stating that they are "symbolic of the English race." He then contrasts them with Nazis, who he claims are finding a new life and vitality by returning to primitive virtues like barbarism. The first speaker states they do not hesitate to destroy in order to create a new world. The other speaker replies, "God help it." A brief musical interlude follows, a suspenseful, atmospheric cue with a low register brass sound.

The clip begins with two male speakers, the first expressing remorse for the second, who is called Thorndike. The second speaker is interrupted by loud, dramatic orchestral music, building intensity. Later, a single male speaker calmly addresses someone, explaining that they can leave the country a free man and return to their position, but on one condition: they must sign a document. The speaker describes the document as something to be witnessed by officials. The addressed party asks if it is a suicide note as the music continues.

The clip starts with a male speaker accusing someone of attempting to assassinate their "Fuhrer" and of undertaking this crime with the approval of their government. The accused sounds incredulous and says, "I, what?" The first man continues, accusing the person of acting as an assassin for the British government, and the second speaker expresses disbelief, stating "I can't believe you're serious." The first male speaker presses further, asking if the accused still claims no intention to shoot. The second speaker replies, claiming it was just a "sporting stalk", so the accuser asks why he did not leave his rifle behind. After a slight pause, the accused expresses he thinks "it wouldn't have been sporting, it wouldn't have been playing the game".

The clip starts with two male speakers discussing the hypocrisy of the English and the concept of "playing the game." One speaker, seemingly more educated, expresses his disillusionment with the idea of fair play, even questioning his own motives, stating it had to be "a loaded rifle with my finger on the trigger." The other speaker warns him. The first speaker then says he means no insult, but asks how he's expected to describe a man who wants to play god and have everyone else run around and say "Heil Hitler." The second speaker warns the first again. Then, there is a noticeable pause. Afterward, melancholic brass music begins, suggesting a somber or reflective mood. Simultaneously, the sounds of a train can be heard, subtly increasing in volume, implying a movement or journey.

The clip starts with a stern male voice pressuring someone to sign a document, declaring that refusal is not an option. A second male voice responds defiantly, stating that it is his decision and reflecting on how easy it is to throw away one's life, then questioning the first voice on their capacity to endure pain. The first voice threatens to let his men do the talking if the second voice refuses to cooperate, offering to save him from their persuasion. The first voice then issues a command in German and the scene is interrupted by the sound of a punch. The music swells—solemn and dramatic—played on strings and organ, evoking a dark and imposing mood.
